newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on corn and soybean drop.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on corn and soybean drop.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on a drop in corn and soybean futures, traders said.
Forecasts for showers this weekend in key U.S. corn and soybean growing states hit those markets, and wheat fell in sympathy. But other factors leaned on wheat prices.

Wheat continued to labor under the weight of reports of a bumper harvest this year in the U.S. winter wheat growing region. The Great Plains hard red winter combining has progressed to near completion in Kansas, the key HRW state, and an excellent crop was harvested.
Also the soft red winter harvest was progressing rapidly amid reports of excellent yields and quality.

Routine exports left the market drifting but there was news early Wednesday that Pakistan next week would seek 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat. Also, Algeria has slated a tender for 75,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat, European grain traders said.
Wheat closed two to seven cents per bushel lower, with July down seven at $3.25 and September down 6-3/4 at $3.31-1/2.
E.D. and F. Man Interntional sold two million bushels of September, Refco Inc sold 2.5 million bushels of September and Farmers Commodities Corp sold one million bushels of March, traders said.
In spread trading, Prudential Securities did 500,000 bushels of December/March at nine cents, premium March, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 17,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 24,501.

In wheat options, Rand Financial sold 500 December $3.90 calls at 7-1/2 to 7-3/4 cents, E.D. and F. Man International bought 500 December $3.80 calls at 9-1/2 to 9-3/4 cents and bought 200 September $3.50 calls at five cents, traders said.
Options volume was pegged at 3,800 contracts, against Tuesday's actual volume of 5,108.
